Module 1: Enterprise Architecture: Tagisan Subsystem 5 & Microsoft Power Platform

### 1.1 Enterprise Architecture: Tagisan Subsystem 5 & Microsoft Power Platform In modern Global 2000 enterprises, software engineering operates at the intersection of developer toolchains and low-code business workflows. Mission-critical business processes, compliance approvals, financial ledgers, and operational incident workflows reside within the **Microsoft Power Platform** and **Microsoft 365 Copilot Substrate** ecosystem. **Tagisan (`tgs`) Subsystem 5** establishes the sovereign bridge between autonomous AI engineering agents and the Microsoft enterprise substrate. Rather than treating low-code platforms as disconnected toys, Tagisan exposes deep, bidirectional, programmatic integration across: 1. **Microsoft Dataverse**: OData v4 Web API engine, transactional batch upserts (`$batch`), delta token synchronization, and entity modeling for Architectural Decision Records (ADRs). 2. **Power Automate**: Cloud flow transpilation (`workflowDefinition.json`), automated Dataverse event triggers, HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks, and Teams Adaptive Card approval loops. 3. **Power Apps Component Framework (PCF)**: Native TypeScript generator synthesizing Fluent UI React controls (`TagisanAstConsensusWidget.tsx`) embedded directly into model-driven forms. 4. **Power BI & Microsoft Fabric**: Real-time push datasets, automated DAX calculation synthesis, OneLake Direct Lake semantic modeling, and Spark notebook execution. 5. **Microsoft Copilot Studio**: Declarative AI plugin manifests, multi-turn conversational topic dialogs, and autonomous tool bindings. 6. **Microsoft Purview & Entra ID**: Zero-trust security, Conditional Access Evaluation (CAE), Continuous Access Evaluation, On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token delegation, and automated DLP sensitivity labeling. ### 1.2 The Sovereign Security Tenet: GCC High & Multi-Tenant Isolation Tagisan is engineered from the ground up to support highly regulated environments, including **commercial Azure**, **Azure Government (GCC High)**, and **Department of Defense (DoD) Impact Level 5/6**: - **Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE)**: Real-time revocation token verification prevents session hijacking even if network egress changes mid-flow. - **Hardware-Enforced Landlock LSM**: Prevents unauthorized credential leaks from local disks. - **Strict Purview Labeling**: All architectural artifacts exported by Tagisan receive encrypted MIP sensitivity tags before entering cloud storage.

Module 2: Installation, Binary Toolchains & Entra ID Authentication Setup

### 2.1 Installation, Binary Toolchains & Entra ID Authentication Setup To connect Tagisan to your Microsoft 365 tenant, configure the Entra ID application registration and verify the connection:
Terminal — Authenticate Tagisan with Entra ID
EXIT 0 • 88ms
prod-sre@tagisan:~$ tgs copilot auth --status
┌───────────────────────────── 🔐 ENTRA ID AUTHENTICATION STATUS ─────────────────────────────┐ │ Tenant ID : 72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47 (Tagisan Enterprise Production) │ │ Client ID : 4a2b91c8-e390-482f-87a1-0987654321ab │ │ Auth Mode : OAuth 2.0 Device Code / WAM Silent SSO │ │ Token Status : Valid (Expires in 58m 22s) │ │ CAE Compliance : Active (Continuous Access Evaluation Verified) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Connected to Microsoft Graph API & Power Platform WebAPI.
### 2.2 Environment Variables Hierarchy Tagisan resolves Microsoft credentials through the following deterministic cascade: 1. `AZURE_TENANT_ID`: The GUID of your Microsoft Entra ID tenant. 2. `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`: The App Registration Application ID. 3. `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` or `AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`: Credentials for daemon/service principal execution. 4. `DATAVERSE_ENVIRONMENT_URL`: Dynamics 365 / Dataverse root URL (e.g. `https://org12345.crm.dynamics.com`).

Module 3: Certified Custom Connectors & OpenAPI 2.0 / `x-ms-*` Metadata

### 3.1 Certified Custom Connectors & OpenAPI 2.0 Specifications Power Apps and Power Automate interact with external REST APIs through **Custom Connectors**. A production-ready custom connector requires: - OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) specification formatted with Microsoft extensions (`x-ms-summary`, `x-ms-visibility`, `x-ms-dynamic-values`). - OAuth 2.0 Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) authentication definition.

Module 5: Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) & Fluent UI React Widgets

### 5.1 Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) & Fluent UI React The **Power Apps Component Framework (PCF)** enables pro-developers to create custom visual UI controls for model-driven and canvas apps. Tagisan synthesizes a complete, production-grade PCF code component: - **`ControlManifest.Input.xml`**: Defines bound properties (`RiskScore`, `ConsensusVerdict`), WebAPI feature usage, and CSS styling. - **`TagisanAstConsensusWidget.tsx`**: A responsive Fluent UI React widget that renders interactive AST dependency graphs and Hegelian debate consensus gauges. - **Lifecycle Implementation (`index.ts`)**: Implements `init`, `updateView`, `getOutputs`, and `destroy`.

Module 8: Power BI Dashboards, DAX Synthesis & Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse

### 8.1 Power BI Dashboards, DAX Synthesis & Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse Tagisan automates the entire analytical lifecycle: 1. **Push Datasets API**: Streams live agent token spend, latency percentiles, and test pass rates into Power BI streaming tiles. 2. **Automated DAX Synthesis**: Generates complex calculations (`MTTR = CALCULATE(AVERAGE(...), FILTER(...))`) without manual formula drafting. 3. **Microsoft Fabric OneLake Integration**: Writes ACID transactional Delta Lake tables directly to OneLake storage for petabyte-scale analysis.

Module 10: Security Governance, Entra ID (OBO/CAE) & Microsoft Purview Compliance

### 10.1 Security Governance, Entra ID & Microsoft Purview Compliance Enterprise software must adhere to strict regulatory compliance: 1. **On-Behalf-Of (OBO) Flow**: Tagisan seamlessly exchanges user credentials for scoped API tokens, preserving auditability. 2. **Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP)**: Automated PII redaction ensures credit cards, passwords, and sensitive keys are stripped before payloads leave the host. 3. **Information Protection (MIP)**: Exported ADRs and solution packages receive cryptographic sensitivity labels (`Confidential / All Employees`).

Module 12: Production Operations, ALM Automation, pac CLI & SRE Monitoring

### 12.1 Production Operations, ALM Automation & SRE Playbooks Automating Power Platform Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) requires headless command execution: 
# Example: Automated Solution Export & Unpack via PAC CLI
pac solution export --name TagisanEnterpriseSolution --path ./solution.zip --managed
pac solution unpack --zipfile ./solution.zip --folder ./src/solutions/TagisanEnterprise/

# Example: Deploying to Production via Tagisan CLI
tgs copilot powerplatform --action deploy_solution --target-env https://tagisan-prod.crm.dynamics.com
